1.

By way of present appeal, challenge has been laid to an award dated 12.02.1999 passed by the Reference Court-cum-Additional District Judge, Jagadhri, whereby reference petition filed at the instance of respondents-landowners invoking Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (herein after referred to as "1894 Act"), stands allowed.

2. Briefly stating, land owned by the respondents-landowners, situated in the revenue estate of village Milkhera, Tehsil Jagadhri, District Jagadhri, came to be acquired vide notification dated 04.02.1987 issued under Section 4 of the 1894 Act, for purposes of constructing link road.
The Land Acquisition Collector, in exercise of its powers under Section 11 of the 1894 Act, assessed the value of the land at the rate of Rs.20,000/- per acre.

sentences.text:
Collector, respondents-landowners invoked reference petition under Section 18 of the 1894 Act,
seeking enhancement of compensation.

Upon consideration of the material available on record, the Reference Court vide its award dated 12.02.1999 decided the reference petition and the relevant paras therefrom are reproduced hereunder:-
" 19.
In view of my findings on issue No.1 and 2 above, present reference accepted.

It is held that the petitioners are entitled to enhance compensation for the acquired land at the rate of Rs.42,500/-
(Rs.Forty two thousand and five hundred) per acre for the acquired land.
However, the petitioners shall not be entitled to anything else for alleged standing trees.

20. The claimants shall also be entitled to solatium at the rate of 30% on the market value as assessed as provided under Section 23(2) of the Act, additional compensation at the rate of 12% per annum as provided under Section 23(IA) of the Act, besides interest as provided under Sectionn 28 of the Act.

21. It is made clear that the compensation now determined shall be subject to payment, if any,
already made by the respondent-State."
4.
By way of present appeal, the aforementioned award dated 12.02.1999 has been assailed at the instance of appellant-State against the enhancement.

5. Learned counsel for the appellant vehemently submits that the enhancement was awarded in favour of landowners by the Reference Court without any basis as no appropriate cut towards development charges was ever imposed upon the appreciated sale price of sale deed (Ex.P-1).

She further submits that the sale deed (Ex.P-1) pertained to only 01 kanal 6 marlas of land and thus,
adequate deduction should have been made on the sale price thereof.
No other argument has been addressed.

Further in the given facts, once the total acquisition was merely for 3.6 acres and the sale deed dated 13.12.1984 (Ex.P-1) pertained to 01 kanal 06 marlas of land with Rs.34,000/- being the price per acre, having applied appreciation of 12% per annum for 2 years i.e. from 13.12.1984 (date of execution of sale deed Ex.P-1) to 04.02.1987 (date of notification under Section 4 of the 1984 Act in the case in hand), the Reference Court committed no illegality or perversity while granting enhancement of Rs.8500/- in favour of respondents-landowners by making the enhanced compensation @ Rs.42,500/- per acre.
9. Accordingly, in terms of the discussion made herein above, finding no merits in the present appeal, the same is thus, dismissed.
10. Considering the fact that no one has appeared on behalf of the respondents-landowners.
